Align and update a list of taxon names in one call

Source: R/create_taxonomic_update_lookup.R
create_taxonomic_update_lookup.Rd

The one-call convenience pipeline: align_taxa() followed by update_taxa(). Matches each name in original_name against resources, then resolves that match forward to its current accepted name.

Usage

create_taxonomic_update_lookup(
  original_name,
  resources = NULL,
  identifier = NA_character_,
  fuzzy_abs_dist = 3,
  fuzzy_rel_dist = 0.2,
  fuzzy_matches = TRUE,
  imprecise_fuzzy_matches = FALSE,
  taxon_ranks_to_check = NULL,
  hybrids = TRUE,
  intergrades_affinis = TRUE,
  consider_english_name_endings = FALSE,
  include_bracketed_info = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE,
  taxonomic_splits = c("most_likely_species", "collapse_to_higher_taxon"),
  full = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

original_name

Character vector of raw taxon names to align and update.

resources

The nested list of reference tibbles produced by prepare_taxonomic_resources(), or a reference table (or list of them) – see align_taxa().

identifier, fuzzy_abs_dist, fuzzy_rel_dist, fuzzy_matches, imprecise_fuzzy_matches, taxon_ranks_to_check, hybrids, intergrades_affinis, consider_english_name_endings, include_bracketed_info, progress

Forwarded to align_taxa(); see its documentation.

taxonomic_splits

Passed to update_taxa(): how to report a name that leads to more than one accepted name ("most_likely_species", the default, or "collapse_to_higher_taxon").

full

Logical; if TRUE, return every intermediate column align_taxa()/update_taxa() compute. If FALSE (the default), return just the key output columns: original_name, aligned_name, accepted_name, suggested_name, genus, family, taxon_rank, taxonomic_dataset, taxonomic_status, taxonomic_status_aligned, aligned_reason, update_reason and chars_changed (the number of characters that differed between the name being matched and the reference name it matched – 0 for an exact match, the edit distance for a fuzzy match, NA when nothing matched).

quiet

Logical; if FALSE (the default), ends by printing a summary, as APCalign's does: how many distinct names aligned to a species or infraspecific taxon (by dataset), only to a genus or a family, or to another rank; how many couldn't be aligned; how many were updated to a different name; and how many could refer to more than one accepted taxon. TRUE prints nothing.

Value

A tibble with one row per element of original_name; see update_taxa() for column details.

Examples

reference <- data.frame(
  canonical_name = c("Boronia", "Boronia serrulata", "Boronia oldname"),
  scientific_name = c("Boronia Sm.", "Boronia serrulata Sm.", "Boronia oldname Sm."),
  taxon_rank = c("genus", "species", "species"),
  taxonomic_status = c("accepted", "accepted", "synonym"),
  taxonomic_dataset = "MY_LIST", genus = "Boronia",
  taxon_ID = c("1", "2", "3"), accepted_name_usage_ID = c("1", "2", "2")
)
create_taxonomic_update_lookup(
  c("Boronia serulata", "Boronia oldname", "Boronia sp."),
  reference
)
#> Summary of 3 names:
#>   -> 2 aligned to a species or infraspecific taxon (2 in MY_LIST)
#>   -> 1 aligned only to a genus and 0 only to a family
#>   -> 0 could not be aligned
#>   -> 1 aligned names were updated to a different name (e.g. a synonym to its accepted name, or an outdated genus to the current one)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 20
#>   original_name    aligned_name    accepted_name suggested_name genus taxon_rank
#>   <chr>            <chr>           <chr>         <chr>          <chr> <chr>     
#> 1 Boronia serulata Boronia serrul… Boronia serr… Boronia serru… Boro… species   
#> 2 Boronia oldname  Boronia oldname Boronia serr… Boronia serru… Boro… species   
#> 3 Boronia sp.      Boronia sp.     Boronia       Boronia sp.    Boro… genus     
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: taxonomic_dataset <chr>, taxonomic_status <chr>,
#> #   scientific_name <chr>, aligned_reason <chr>, update_reason <chr>,
#> #   number_of_collapsed_taxa <int>, chars_changed <int>, taxon_ID <chr>,
#> #   taxon_ID_genus <chr>, scientific_name_ID <chr>, family <chr>,
#> #   taxonomic_status_aligned <chr>, alternative_possible_names <chr>,
#> #   identifier <chr>
